definitions.explanation: A formal honorific term of address used to address a group of people respectfully. Commonly used in business emails, official notices, and formal announcements. Equivalent to "Dear all" or "To whom it may concern."

examples.japanese: {関係者|かんけいしゃ}{各位|かくい}
{社員|しゃいん}{各位|かくい}にお{知|し}らせいたします。
examples.english: We would like to inform all employees.

examples.japanese: {会員|かいいん}{各位|かくい}におかれましては、ますますご{健勝|けんしょう}のこととお{慶|よろこ}び{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: We are pleased to hope that all members are in good health.

notes:
USAGE:
{各位|かくい} is itself an honorific, so adding さま or {殿|どの} after it is considered redundant, though {各位|かくい}さま is sometimes seen in practice. Typically placed after a group noun: {社員|しゃいん}{各位|かくい}, {会員|かいいん}{各位|かくい}, {関係者|かんけいしゃ}{各位|かくい}. Used primarily in written communication — business emails, notices, and circulars.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社員|しゃいん}{各位|かくい}: to all employees
- {会員|かいいん}{各位|かくい}: to all members
- {関係者|かんけいしゃ}{各位|かくい}: to all concerned parties
- {保護者|ほごしゃ}{各位|かくい}: to all parents/guardians
